name: Number input
description: A field for entering a number, often with minus and plus buttons that step the value. Use it for amounts people count, such as a quantity; for digit strings like postcodes, use a Text input.
summary: Enter or step a number, such as a quantity

elements.name: Field
elements.description: Holds the typed value; respects min, max and step

elements.name: Step buttons
elements.description: Minus and plus buttons with names such as "Decrease quantity"

elements.name: Hint text
elements.description: The allowed range or unit, such as "1 to 10"

elements.name: Error message
elements.description: Says what is allowed, such as "Quantity must be 10 or fewer"

configOptions.options: None, Both sides, Stacked at the end

variants.caption: Plain — field only, no step buttons
variants.htmlOutline:
<label for="qty">Quantity</label>
<input id="qty" type="text" inputmode="numeric" pattern="[0-9]*" value="1">
<!-- a text field with a numeric keyboard, without the browser's spin buttons -->

variants.caption: Stacked — small up and down buttons at the end
Unit — suffix inside the field
variants.htmlOutline: kg

usageNotes: This is the quantity control that is sometimes called a stepper. A sequence of numbered stages in a process is Steps.
Use type="number" only for amounts. Card numbers, postcodes and phone numbers aren't counted; use a Text input with inputmode="numeric".
Set min, max and step, and state the limits in the hint so people know them before they see an error.
Custom versions follow the APG Spinbutton pattern: role="spinbutton" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax, Up and Down arrows to step, and typing still allowed.
Give the minus and plus buttons accessible names, such as "Decrease quantity", and targets of at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels (WCAG 2.5.8).
htmlOutline:
<label for="qty">Quantity</label>
<input id="qty" type="number" min="1" max="10" value="1">
